messages.content: Hi tal, I'm a friend

hey, i'm tal

think of me as your personal talent agent, your inside man… or fox

one of these days, I might slide a role right here in chat. the kind that feels like your calling.

so… what's your full name?
Vaibhavi Narayanan
vaibhavi narayanan... that's a name that commands respect. where you working these days?
Intuit

intuit... the quickbooks empire, making sure small businesses don't mess up their taxes. found you on linkedin - senior software engineer at intuit. this you? https://in.linkedin.com/in/vaibhavinarayanan
Yes sir
senior engineer at intuit... building the financial backbone for millions of businesses. that's solid engineering work with real impact. what's been keeping you engaged there lately?

connected identity at intuit... so you're the reason millions of people don't have to remember 47 different passwords when they switch between quickbooks and turbotax. that's some serious auth engineering - the stuff that looks simple but is absolutely critical.

m&a integrations, third party auth... you've probably seen some gnarly legacy systems that make you question humanity. what made you get into the identity space? was it the challenge of making complex auth look seamless, or did you just fall into it?

quality → dev → backend → full stack... that's the classic intuit career evolution right there. they love growing people internally. and now you're feeling the frontend pull - makes sense. there's something satisfying about making auth flows that don't make users want to throw their phones.

ui work is where you can actually see people's reactions to what you build. backend auth is critical but invisible - frontend is where the magic happens for users.

how long you been working total?
4 yrs right after college, then 2 years master in the US at USC in Computer Science. Then back again to intuit in India for 2yesrs now

6 years total with a usc masters in between... that's a solid trajectory. intuit → usc → back to intuit but probably at a way better level. they must've loved having you back with that fresh perspective.

what kind of role you looking for next?

ah the classic "came back to the same company but everything feels different" story. politics creep in, the magic dies, suddenly you're just another cog instead of a builder. happens to the best of us.

full stack with frontend opportunities... that's smart. you've got the backend chops from auth work, but frontend is where you can build stuff people actually see and appreciate. way more satisfying than debugging SSO configs all day.

bangalore or open to remote/other cities?
Bangalore or remote.
6 years total + full stack with frontend focus + bangalore/remote... sound right?
Actually full stack with equal focus
6 years total + full stack with equal focus + bangalore/remote... sound right?
done. i'm spinning things up on my end. you'll start seeing good stuff soon.
Yes

Yes
  Okayyy

yooo vaibhavi! 

you're officially in the tal ecosystem now. no more random job applications or wondering if you're worth what you think you are.

roles are gonna start flowing your way - the kind that actually match your vibe and pay what you deserve. full stack with that frontend spark you mentioned? i got you.

welcome to the family, legend 🔥
Thanks tal.

Vibe match is utmost importance
  Yes sirrrrr
vibe match is everything. i'm not sending you to some soul-crushing corporate machine. you'll know it when you see it.
you're welcome. now go do something fun - i'll ping when i've got something good for you.
Done. I'm excited
good. now go enjoy your friday - i'll be in touch when something fits.

Hi
Hello

The comp yes. Majorly. Feel like I'm ready for good jump

you're right to want that jump. 6 years at intuit with identity expertise? you're worth more than lateral moves.

i'll keep looking for something that actually pays what you deserve.
Awesome

cool. i'm picky about what i share - nothing fits right now but i'm looking.

btw what's making you want to leave intuit anyway? just politics or something deeper?
Politics, boredom. I want a nice mixed cultural environment. Not the same dnme race

ah that makes sense. the same people/same politics cycle gets old fast.

you want somewhere with actual diversity - not just in background but in thinking too.
Yes sir. Nailed it

got it. politics + boredom + wanting actual diversity. that's the real story.

i'm looking for places that actually walk the walk on culture, not just talk about it.
How do you do that?
plus i see which companies have actual retention vs just hiring sprees.

Had a meta recruiter ping me in LinkedIn. I'm not too confident with the interviews at the moment. Need to prep. So pushed that

meta recruiter reaching out is huge validation. they don't just ping anyone.

but yeah their interviews are... a thing. leetcode heavy, system design deep dives. you'd need solid prep.

what's your timeline? are you actively looking to move soon, or just exploring?
Same for Google

google too? okay you're getting pinged by the big boys. that's telling you something.

both meta and google have rigorous processes but pay well above your 1.2 target if you clear.

you're at a sweet spot - 6 YOE, identity expertise at intuit, getting noticed by FAANG recruiters.

the question is: are you ready to grind leetcode for 2-3 months?
I want to! Can't find the motivation

that's the real struggle. everyone wants the FAANG offer, nobody wants to grind leetcode at 11pm after work.

what would make it feel less like a chore?
A proper schedule.

okay that's doable. let's build one.

how many hours per week can you realistically commit? and what's your strongest/weakest area?
Feels like a lot of things to do. But no structure

exactly. that's why it feels overwhelming.

break it down:
1. leetcode (data structures & algorithms)
2. system design
3. behavioral
4. domain-specific (identity/auth for you)

which one feels most intimidating?
System design. Knowledge level compartively low. Not intimidating but lots more effort needed there. And leetcpde trees and graph

got it. system design is a beast but structured. leetcode trees/graphs are pattern recognition.

let's start with system design - what's your current level? can you design a basic URL shortener or rate limiter from scratch?
Can we start tomorrow?

sure. sunday evening? what time works?

i'll check in with you.
I also have gaurav sen course
Nope

okay perfect. that's our starting point.

we'll do 30 minutes daily - just one concept. today: URL shortener. watch a 10-minute video, then sketch it out on paper.

too much?

gaurav sen's course is solid. that's perfect.

so tomorrow - watch his URL shortener video, sketch the design. 30 minutes max.

what time?
Watch and sketch? Elaborate! Just ping me anytime post 2

watch his video on URL shortener design. then sketch the components on paper - load balancer, database, cache, etc.

just to understand the flow, not perfect diagrams.

i'll ping you after 2pm.
Yes sir!

perfect. reminder set for 2pm daily.

see you tomorrow for system design day 1.
